claimMap.claim: loans vary a lot in the amount you can borrow, whether you need to provide security, and their costs and conditions
claimMap.sourceText: Loans vary a lot in their costs and conditions, including: the amount you can borrow ... Read each loan's terms and conditions carefully to compare: ... minimum and maximum loan amounts ... whether you need to provide security ... upfront and ongoing charges

claimMap.claim: Lenders may ask for details of the property, any lease and your business finances
claimMap.sourceText: A secured loan is backed up by collateral or security ... such as property ... you may need to provide: ... financial reports, including cash flow statements ... financial forecasts ... lease agreements ... your personal financial information

claimMap.claim: Budget for set-up costs and other upfront fees that the lender discloses
claimMap.sourceText: set-up costs and ongoing fees ... upfront and ongoing charges

claimMap.claim: the buyer generally pays transfer (stamp) duty on a purchase
claimMap.sourceText: NSW: When you buy a property or someone transfers ownership of a property to you in NSW, you generally must pay transfer duty (stamp duty). QLD: The buyer - whether an individual, first home buyer, investor, business or foreign purchaser - is usually responsible for paying transfer (stamp) duty ... rates apply to ... commercial properties.

claimMap.claim: Victoria also charges land transfer duty
claimMap.sourceText: You pay land transfer duty when buying property in Victoria ... Land transfer duty is paid when property is bought or acquired in Victoria. It applies to all property types, including those that have not yet transitioned to the commercial and industrial property tax reform.

claimMap.claim: Victoria is progressively replacing land transfer and landholder duty on commercial and industrial property with an annual commercial and industrial property tax (CIPT)
claimMap.sourceText: A tax progressively replacing land transfer and landholder duty ... Commercial and industrial property tax (CIPT) is an annual tax on the land value of commercial and industrial properties in Victoria.

claimMap.claim: CIPT is payable 10 years after the property enters the reform
claimMap.sourceText: Overview: It is payable 10 years after the property enters the CIPT reform. Assessments: You may need to pay ... if you own a commercial or industrial property that has entered the CIPT reform and completed its 10-year transition period. The earliest CIPT assessment year is 2035.

claimMap.claim: Whether a later dealing is exempt from duty depends on that transaction, including whether it is a tax reform scheme transaction and whether the property has a qualifying use
claimMap.sourceText: A dutiable transaction involving a property that has entered the commercial and industrial property tax (CIPT) reform may be exempt from land transfer duty (also known as stamp duty) if it is a 'tax reform scheme transaction' that meets certain criteria including that the property has a qualifying use. Different exemption criteria apply to standard and non-standard transactions.

claimMap.claim: financial reports, forecasts and lease agreements among documents you may need to provide
claimMap.sourceText: Documentation requirements vary between loans, but you may need to provide: ... financial reports, including cash flow statements (if available) ... financial forecasts ... lease agreements

claimMap.claim: comparing products from multiple lenders, including non-bank lenders, because costs and conditions vary
claimMap.sourceText: It's a good idea to compare loan products from multiple lenders before applying. ... Check for loans from non-bank lenders as well as traditional banks. Read each loan's terms and conditions carefully to compare: upfront and ongoing charges ... whether you need to provide security
